title: On Light-beams Breaking from Above
description: On Light-beams Breaking from Above in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 620 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: On light beams break-ing from a-bove, Th'e-ter-nal course of mer-cy runs; And by ten thou-sand cords of love Our heav-enly Fa-ther guides his sons.

lines: The eternal course of mercy runs;
And by ten thousand cords of love
Our heavenly Father guides his sons.
The heavenly cord is drawn the most,
And most is felt the heavenly hand.
Oh, be it mine to feel, to see
Through earth's perplexed and varying road,
The cords that link us, God, to thee,
And draw us to thine own abode.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
